candidates.api_shape: cone_clutch(d, cone_deg, face_w, bore_d, engage_frac, clearance) -> {male, female} posed on +Z
candidates.fdm: Two mating frustums. Print the male standing (self-supporting under ~45 deg) or split. engage_frac withdraws the male the way dog_clutch does. PLA-on-PLA is a real friction pair at teaching torque; a felt or TPU liner is an optional argument, not a second kit.
candidates.name: cone_clutch
candidates.why: Wedge-amplified friction clutch: male and female cones, axial engage. Textbook sibling of the plate clutch (Norton) and the printable synchro. Higher torque than a same-diameter disc. frustum is the solid, not the clutch. Not a dog (positive) and not a plate pack.

candidates.api_shape: wrap_spring_clutch(hub_d, width, spring_turns, wire, control='free'|locked, sense) -> {input_hub, output_hub, spring}
candidates.fdm: Two printed hubs, close-fit helix. Printed TPU or thin PETG coil demos the capstan lock; a bought clock spring is the working option. coil_spring is the blank, not the clutch (no second hub, no wrap diameter, no control tang).
candidates.name: wrap_spring_clutch
candidates.why: Helix wrapped on two coaxial hubs. Drive that tightens the spring locks (capstan, torque ~ e^{mu*theta}); the other sense unwraps and slips. Creed single-turn, Pitney Bowes, Thomson CB, printing-press start-stop. Distinct from coil_spring and from every ratchet. Same wrapping pair as a band, on a helix.

candidates.api_shape: centrifugal_clutch(drum_id, shoes=2, shoe_mass_proxy, spring_preload, rpm_or_frac) -> {hub, shoes, springs, drum}
candidates.fdm: Hub with pivots, two or three shoes with printed friction faces, extension springs (coil_spring or a printed flexure), outer drum. Pose by engage_frac or a reported engagement rpm. Prints as a kit; shoes print flat.
candidates.name: centrifugal_clutch
candidates.why: Speed-actuated expanding shoes inside a drum. Chainsaws, go-karts, mopeds, lawn equipment: idle is free, a trip rpm couples the drum. Drum brake in reverse. No current API engages by speed. Not a dog and not a roller freewheel.

candidates.api_shape: band_brake(drum_d, width, wrap_deg, lever_len, apply_frac) -> {drum, band, lever} plus band_brake_ratio(mu, wrap_deg)
candidates.fdm: Printed drum, a thin printed (or webbing) strap, a lever that shortens the free end. 507 #242. Band can be a printed ribbon at demo scale or a slot that takes bought webbing. First wrapping-pair brake.
candidates.name: band_brake
candidates.why: Flexible band tightens on a drum. Winches, cranes, chainsaws, epicyclic hold, bicycle band brakes, Prony. Effectiveness e^{mu*theta}. Catalog has zero brakes. The wrapping higher pair mechlib never named. Distinct from a shoe (rigid arc) and from wrap-spring (helix on a hub, clutch not brake).

candidates.api_shape: parking_pawl(teeth, tip_r, tooth_h, thickness, overcenter_deg) -> {park_gear, pawl} plus parking_pawl_pose(engaged)
candidates.fdm: Sawtooth or square park gear plus a sprung pawl that seats into a valley and takes torque both ways. Prints flat. Optional over-center on the actuator (toggle_clamp kinematics, not a second clamp).
candidates.name: parking_pawl
candidates.why: Positive lock of a shaft to ground. Transmission park, hoist pawl, over-center park brake. A ratchet drives one way and clicks the other; a park pawl holds both directions and is not in the drive path when lifted. ratchet_wheel_pawl is the winch drive, not the park.

candidates.api_shape: sprag_clutch(n, hub_r, sprag_l, race_r, height, tilt_deg) -> {hub, race, sprags}
candidates.fdm: Two smooth cylinders plus n figure-8 (or cam) sprags posed at the lock tilt. Prints. Wear is ugly without a bought needle or a TPU sprag; still a valid geometry kit. Not a drop-in roller.
candidates.name: sprag_clutch
candidates.why: Overrunning clutch whose elements are asymmetric cams that stay in contact with both races and wedge by tilting. Helicopter autorotation, starter overrun, conveyor backstop, auto 1-2. Distinct from freewheel_clutch: rollers leave a ramped pocket; sprags never leave the races. The prompt listed this as missing; it is.

candidates.api_shape: expanding_shoe_brake(drum_id, shoe_arc_deg, pivot, apply_frac) -> {drum, shoe_a, shoe_b, actuator}
candidates.fdm: Two rigid shoes on pivots inside a drum, cam or linkage spreads them. Prints flat. Same shoe primitive as centrifugal_clutch; actuation is a lever, not rpm.
candidates.name: expanding_shoe_brake
candidates.why: Internal-expanding drum brake. Automotive drum, hoist service brake, any shaft-to-ground friction that is not a band. 507 has the external strap (242) but not the internal pair. Shares shoes with centrifugal; do not emit a third shoe kit.

candidates.api_shape: single_rev_clutch(hub_d, trip='spring'|'pawl', phase_deg) -> {input, output, trip} plus single_rev_engaged(theta)
candidates.fdm: Wrap-spring hubs plus a trip cam/tang, or a cascaded-pawl disc (Teletype / Selectric). Prints. Pose is crank angle through one turn then lock.
candidates.name: single_revolution_clutch
candidates.why: One pull, one turn, then it parks. Presses, shears, teleprinters, postage meters, typewriters. Not a generic wrap-spring (which stays locked while driven) and not a Geneva (which indexes a load from a continuously spinning crank). The trip is the primitive.

candidates.fdm: Same two hubs as dog_clutch; the tooth face is a helix so relative rotation walks the jaws into mesh. Prints standing or as a loft.
candidates.name: spiral_jaw_clutch
candidates.why: Self-engaging jaw: spiral faces pull the clutch in under torque. Square-jaw is already dog_clutch. Spiral-jaw is the other named positive clutch (machine-tool back-gear, some PTO). A jaw= argument, not a second module, but the geometry is missing.

candidates.api_shape: ball_ramp(n, pitch_r, ramp_h, ball_d, twist_deg) -> {plate_a, plate_b, balls} axial gap = f(twist)
candidates.fdm: Two discs with opposed ramps, n printed or bought balls. Twist makes axial clamp. Prints flat. Clearance is the only hard parameter.
candidates.name: ball_ramp_clutch
candidates.why: Relative rotation rides balls up ramps and generates axial force. Locking diffs, some torque limiters, clutch actuators. Not freewheel_clutch (radial wedge, one-way) and not torque_limiter (detent bumps, no balls). The prompt's roller-ramp is the radial freewheel; this is the axial cousin.

candidates.api_shape: prefer centrifugal_clutch(shoes='foa') over a second kit; FOA is two printed parts, no coil springs
candidates.fdm: BYU Floating-Opposing-Arm: two printed bodies, flexure arms fling out. Thingiverse 3007264. Prints as a pair. Same job as centrifugal_clutch, Howell construction.
candidates.name: compliant_centrifugal
candidates.why: Howell's missing clutch sibling. compliant_clutch is an overrunning/limiter flexure, not a speed-actuated shoe. Do not add a fifth clutch module if centrifugal_clutch can emit an FOA shoe style.

candidates.api_shape: multiplate_pack(n, od, id, t, basket_lugs, hub_lugs) -> {steels, frictions, basket, hub}
candidates.fdm: Alternating discs with outer/inner lugs. Prints. Real friction wants bought paper or cork; printed-on-printed is a teaching stack. Basket+hub+pressure plate is close to a motorcycle clutch, i.e. a product.
candidates.name: multiplate_pack
candidates.why: Wet multi-disc: n friction + n steel. Motorcycle, auto clutch packs, DCT. The pack is a primitive; the basket is a product. After cone_clutch exists this is a stack helper, not a new family.

candidates.api_shape: two annular faces + axial spring; or cone_clutch held at partial engage_frac
candidates.fdm: Printed faces slip continuously. Heat and wear are the point. torque_limiter already trips by detent; this would slip smoothly.
candidates.name: friction_slip_clutch
candidates.why: Continuous-slip friction limiter (not a ratchet-past-detents). Useful, but cone_clutch or a plate pair plus belleville_washer already compose it. Do not add until cone exists and someone still asks.

candidates.api_shape: disc_caliper(rotor_od, pad_area, apply_frac) -> {rotor, pad_a, pad_b, carrier}
candidates.fdm: A disc plus two pads on a floating carrier. Prints. A hydraulic opposed-piston caliper is a product (seals, pistons, fluid). Demo-scale mechanical scissor caliper is a kit.
candidates.name: disc_caliper
candidates.why: Shaft-to-ground friction on a disc face. Bicycle mechanical disc, park brake on a rotor. The rotor+pads are semi-primitive; the automotive caliper body is not. Rank below band and expanding-shoe.

candidates.api_shape: compose cone_clutch + dog_clutch blocker teeth; do not add a gearbox product
candidates.fdm: A thin cone with blocking teeth. Prints. The rest of a synchro hub is a product.
candidates.name: synchromesh_ring
candidates.why: Baulk-ring synchro is a cone clutch that must lock before dogs can pass. The primitive is cone_clutch. The gearbox is a product.

candidates.name: roller_ramp_freewheel
candidates.why: Already freewheel_clutch: cylindrical rollers in ramped outer-ring pockets, hub, posed at the free end. The prompt listed roller-ramp as missing; it is the existing overrunning kit.

candidates.fdm: Prints a magnet cage. Working surface is bought magnets or a coil.
candidates.name: magnetic_clutch
candidates.why: Electromagnetic, particle, hysteresis, eddy. Field devices. Same reject as magnetic_gear. A printed magnet holder is a project fixture.

candidates.fdm: Shells print; they do not pump enough to be a clutch.
candidates.name: fluid_coupling
candidates.why: Impeller + turbine (+ stator = torque converter). Working fluid is the clutch. Teaching cutaways are products. The fluid-machines slice owns pumps.

new_categories.name: brakes
new_categories.why: A brake grounds a shaft; a clutch joins two shafts. Winch hold, hoist, park, and Prony are a different agent job from dog/freewheel/limiter. Catalog has a clutches shelf and no brakes shelf. Band, expanding-shoe, and parking-pawl would live here; the missing-categories slice can rank the shelf.

rejected.name: dog_clutch_again
rejected.why: Already dog_clutch. 507 #48 clutch-box is this kit. Spiral-jaw is the missing tooth, not a second dog.

rejected.name: hirth_as_clutch
rejected.why: hirth_coupling is a face-tooth coupling, always meshed. A clutch must be able to part. Do not re-file Hirth under clutches.

rejected.name: needle_roller_one_way
rejected.why: Drawn-cup HF/HFL. Buy the bearing. Printed sprag_clutch is the geometry; the cup is hardware.

rejected.name: automotive_caliper
rejected.why: Opposed-piston hydraulic caliper, seals, fluid, bleed. Product. disc_caliper above is only the rotor+pad kit.

rejected.name: torque_converter
rejected.why: Three-element hydrodynamic coupling plus lock-up clutch. Vehicle powertrain product.

rejected.name: belt_clutch
rejected.why: Slack belt plus an idler that tensions. Already idler_pulley + eccentric_idler_mount.

rejected.name: slipper_clutch
rejected.why: Motorcycle back-torque limiter: multiplate + ramp. Product built from multiplate_pack + ball_ramp.

rejected.name: pin_stud_clutch
rejected.why: 507 #52 and #361: a pin into a hole. Too thin for a kit; dog_clutch with dogs=1 is the same idea.

rejected.name: reversing_double_clutch
rejected.why: 507 #53: two clutch-boxes + three bevels. Assembly of dog_clutch + bevel_gear_pair.

rejected.name: prony_brake
rejected.why: Band brake plus a lever and a scale. Instrument product. band_brake is the primitive.

sources: mechlib/clutches.py (dog_clutch, freewheel_clutch, torque_limiter), mechlib/ratchets.py (compliant_clutch, ratchet_wheel_pawl, pip/cartridge/arc), mechlib/couplings.py (hirth_coupling), mechlib/linkages.py (toggle_clamp), mechlib/flexures.py (coil_spring, belleville, wave_spring), mechlib/prim.py (frustum), mechlib/usecases.py
summary:
A clutch joins two rotating members so they can share torque or part; a brake joins a rotating member to ground. Same physics, different grounding. First split is how torque is made: positive teeth (no slip once seated), friction (can slip, heat is the cost), wrapping/capstan (a helix or strap self-tightens), or fluid/field (bought hardware). Second split is when it happens: operator (lever, pedal), speed (centrifugal), one-way overrun, trip-at-torque, or single-revolution. Reuleaux puts wrapping (band, wrap-spring) in the higher-pair wrapping family; Norton's machine-design chapter treats cone, plate, centrifugal, and band as the textbook set; 507 Movements names clutch-boxes at 47 (friction), 48 (jaw), 52 (stud-in-hole), 53 (reversing double-clutch + bevels), 361 (pin-on-pulley), and the only named brake at 242 (strap on a crane wheel). Howell's printable siblings are the already-shipped compliant flexure clutch (Roach 2003) and the missing FOA centrifugal (BYU CMR).

Catalog already covers four clutch jobs and none of the brake jobs. Positive: dog_clutch (axial rectangular teeth, engage_frac) and hirth_coupling (face-tooth, a coupling not a clutch). Overrunning: freewheel_clutch is a roller-ramp (star pockets + cylindrical rollers; the prompt's 'missing' roller-ramp already exists), plus the ratchet shelf (ratchet_wheel_pawl, pip_ratchet_hub, spring_cartridge_ratchet, arc_ratchet, ratchet_ring). Slip: torque_limiter (spring-detent face bumps) and compliant_clutch (flexure arms vs sawtooth race; lock_face_frac flips one-way vs limiter). Actuation cousins, not clutches: toggle_clamp (over-center knee), eccentric_cam_clamp, detent_pair, flywheel, coil_spring / belleville_washer / wave_spring (the last two already mention clutch-pack take-up), frustum (the cone solid, not a clutch), idler_pulley + eccentric_idler_mount (a belt clutch is just an idler that tensions). Grep of mechlib/ finds no sprag, wrap_spring, cone_clutch, centrifugal, multiplate, band_brake, caliper, parking_pawl, or any brake_* API. The clutches gallery shelf blurb is 'Torque limiting and freewheeling'; there is no brakes shelf.

FDM reality. Cone is two frustums with engage_frac; PLA-on-PLA friction is enough for teaching and light torque, and it is the printable synchro. Wrap-spring is two hubs plus a close-fit helix (printed TPU/PETG coil, or a bought clock spring); torque follows the capstan equation and coil_spring already exists as the spring blank. Centrifugal shoes inside a drum are the go-kart/chainsaw kit; BYU's two-piece FOA prints without coil springs. Band brake is a drum plus a wrapping strap plus a lever (507 #242); first brake primitive, and the wrapping pair mechlib never named. Parking pawl is a both-ways lock into a park gear, not a ratchet. Sprag is figure-8 cams between two smooth races: distinct from roller-ramp (sprags stay in contact both ways; rollers leave the pocket) and printable as a demo, ugly in wear. Expanding-shoe / drum shares shoes with centrifugal and is the internal-expanding brake. Single-revolution wrap-spring (Creed / Pitney Bowes / Teletype) is wrap-spring plus a trip cam. Spiral-jaw is the self-engaging dog tooth. Ball-ramp turns relative rotation into axial clamp (lockers, some limiters), not the same as freewheel_clutch's roller-ramp. Multiplate, single-disc, and disc/caliper are real machines but the working surface is a bought pad or a product housing; emit a pack or a floating-caliper kit only after the cone and band exist. Magnetic, particle, hysteresis, eddy, electromagnetic coils, fluid couplings, and torque converters are not printable working surfaces. Needle-roller HF cups are bought bearings. Automotive synchromesh, slipper clutches, and DCT packs are products built from the primitives above.
title: Clutches, brakes, and overrunning
